result.notes:
All 36 dereference sites in net.rs were reviewed. Findings: 35 genuine user-pointer sites need fixing (raw core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping or core::slice::from_raw_parts[_mut] over a syscall address arg, none mapping-validated). 1 site (sys_tcp_recv, line 365) is already safe via copy_to_user_bytes and is the correct template to follow.

No kernel-internal (not_user_pointer) sites exist in this file — every raw pointer here originates from a syscall u64 address argument (buf_ptr / params_ptr / ip_ptr / result_ptr / data_ptr decoded from a user params struct).

read_user_str call sites (line 304 sys_net_dns, line 1077 sys_net_dns6) are NOT listed as problems: read_user_str internally calls is_user_page_accessible at the start and at every page boundary, so it is already mapping-safe. data_ptr in sys_udp_sendto/sys_udp_sendto_v6 is itself read from the user params struct (32-bit), so it is a user pointer and must be copied via copy_user_bytes after the params struct is safely copied.

Length-is-user-controlled sites to bound carefully: line 349 sys_tcp_send (UNBOUNDED today — highest priority; clamp like TCP_RECV_COPY_CHUNK), line 615/691 udp recvfrom (buf_len; copy only the populated `total` bytes), line 855 sys_net_arp (buf_size; clamp to entries.len()), and lines 121/492/572/660/737/937 (bounded by an explicit cap or by a kernel-side .len() min).

Helper signatures used: copy_user_bytes(ptr,len,max_len)->Option<Vec<u8>>; copy_to_user_bytes(ptr,&[u8],max_len)->bool. Both reject ptr+len overflow and probe every crossed page, so buf_ptr+4 style arithmetic (line 121) is safe through them.

Genuine user-pointer trust-boundary bugs are in TWO functions: sys_fstat and sys_pipe2.

sys_fstat (3 raw *mut u32 store blocks at lines 572-578, 591-597, 607-617): buf_ptr (arg2) is dereferenced with NO mapping check at all — only `if buf_ptr == 0` at line 554. All three write a fixed 16-byte stat struct. Each must be replaced with a local [u8;16] built via to_le_bytes() + copy_to_user_bytes(buf_ptr, &out, 16).

sys_pipe2 (raw *mut u32 store block at lines 719-723): pipefd_ptr is guarded only by is_valid_user_ptr (line 676), which is RANGE-ONLY (confirmed in helpers.rs lines 53-63: checks ptr!=0 and ptr+len<=0x0000_8000_0000_0000, does NOT verify the page is mapped). IMPORTANT: by the time of the write both FDs are allocated and the pipe is created, so the failure path must close read_fd/write_fd and decref the pipe to avoid an FD/pipe leak.

result.notes:
All eight dereference sites operate on genuine USER pointers (syscall address args: buf_ptr / entry_ptr) and are currently guarded ONLY by `is_valid_user_ptr`, a range-only check that the task spec explicitly states is insufficient because it does not verify the page is mapped. None are guarded by the mapping-validated helpers, so all are real trust-boundary bugs. No kind=not_user_pointer sites exist in this file — every raw slice/deref here is on a user address.

Kernel-internal pointers that are correctly NOT flagged: the `sector_buf`/`mbr`/`kbuf` kernel stack/heap buffers (e.g. `[0u8; 512]` at lines 109, 331, 388), the `read_sectors`/`write_sectors` closures, and the `partition::scan_disk` callback all operate on kernel-owned memory, not user pointers, and must stay as-is.

Length-bounding caveat: in sys_disk_read/sys_disk_write, `needed = count * 512` is user-controlled and currently only bounded by the requirement `needed <= buf_size`. Since buf_size is u32, needed is bounded to < 4 GiB, which is still far too large to allocate as a kernel buffer safely. When adopting copy_user_bytes/copy_to_user_bytes (which require a kernel-side buffer), add an explicit upper bound on `count` (or `needed`) to a sane maximum (e.g. a few MiB / a fixed max sector count) before allocating, to avoid a large-allocation DoS.

The DS/ES restoration and other ABI concerns from CLAUDE.md are not relevant to these pointer-safety fixes.

result.notes:
Root cause shared by all 8 vulnerable sites: they gate on `is_valid_user_ptr` (range-only: checks ptr != 0 and ptr+len <= 0x0000_8000_0000_0000) and then do a raw `core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping` / `core::slice::from_raw_parts[_mut]` / `*ptr.add(i)`. Per helpers.rs lines 50-63, `is_valid_user_ptr` does NOT probe page mappings, so any unmapped (or demand-paged-not-yet-faulted) page in the range causes a kernel #PF -> panic. The fix in every case is: build the payload in a kernel-owned buffer (local [u8; N] for fixed structs, Vec<u8> for variable counts) and transfer via `copy_to_user_bytes` (writes) or `copy_user_bytes` (reads), which call `is_user_range_accessible` to probe the first page + every crossed boundary (helpers.rs 84-101).

Vulnerable user-pointer sites (need fixing): monitor.rs lines 61, 90, 117; ipc.rs lines 31, 46, 69; platform.rs line 39; device.rs line 17.

Length is user-controlled (must stay bounded by the temp-buffer cap) at: ipc.rs:31 (len), ipc.rs:46 (len), ipc.rs:69 (buf_size), platform.rs:39 (max_count), monitor.rs:90 (buf_len), monitor.rs:117 (buf_len, controls write_count), device.rs:17 (buf_size). monitor.rs:61 writes a fixed 92-byte struct (length not user-controlled, but mapping still unchecked).

Already-safe sites (read_user_str / copy_user_bytes / copy_to_user_bytes are mapping-validated): ipc.rs 19, 55, 122, 142, 155, 180, 204; device.rs 54, 111, 122/150.

Not-user-pointer: device.rs sys_dll_load `mapped` (kernel-arranged DLL base, line 122 and 150) and sys_set_dll_u32 (no raw deref; validation lives in crate::task::dll). platform.rs I2C/ACPI handlers (sys_i2c_read/write/detect, sys_acpi_sleep/perf, sys_thermal_cpu) take only scalar args — no pointers. monitor.rs sys_monitor_count takes no args. The kernel-internal source pointers `info.edid_raw.as_ptr()` (monitor.rs:91) and `info.modes[i]` fields are fine; only their user destinations are the problem.

Minor extra observation (not a trust-boundary deref): monitor.rs:20 validates 128 bytes but the struct/copy is 92 bytes — harmless over-validation, but worth aligning to size_of when adopting copy_to_user_bytes (it validates exactly the bytes written).
